outcome: Answer a declaration that names the same column as both carried and organizing with the fact of what that means, so the agent can see the consequence of its own declaration without the backend judging it
criteria: A declaration naming a column in both columns and order_by or the one_per keys answers with a fact saying the file will carry it, and that naming it only in order_by or one_per still sorts and counts by it while leaving it out of the file
The fact is neutral: both readings stay legal, a column named in both is still carried exactly as declared, and no declaration is refused or changed by this
Every declared name reports which organizing field named it, if any, whether or not the answer carries it
The existing name facts still fire, framing.py and the MCP tool descriptions are untouched, and the test suite passes

note: declare_output now answers each declared name with which organizing field named it, and a name given both as a carried column and in order_by or the one_per keys is answered with what that means: the file will carry it, and naming it only as organizing would order or set the grain of the answer without writing it. The sentence states the consequence and both readings; it recommends neither, because a column that is ordered by and carried is simply carried (MADR 0012) and some answers do want the sort key in the file. Nothing about the contract changed: no declaration is refused, reshaped or reordered by this, and the locator fact and the both-lists fact are said together when both apply. Four tests in tests/test_contracts.py cover the order_by case, the one_per case, both fields at once, a non-carried organizing name (which reports the field and says nothing further), and the two facts combining; 212 tests pass and examples/demo.py runs. framing.py and the MCP tool descriptions are deliberately untouched so the next DataSpace measurement moves one variable. This addresses the 2026-09-09 measurement finding that four of five runs named the same key in both lists, reading them as additive rather than as a relocation.
